metadata.title: AI-Era 'Super High Schoolers,' a Third Path Beyond College, and China's Innovative Education | Visiting Beijing Tanyue School
metadata.guest: Jason Wang, Jiang Xueqin, Tanyue students and faculty
metadata.guest_role: Tanyue School founder · Western philosophy teacher · Current and graduated learners

conclusion: SV101 spends two days at Beijing Tanyue School — a ten-year competency experiment with ~500 students, tuition above 200,000 RMB, and no fixed classrooms. Jiang Xueqin went viral for classroom forecasts; 17-year-old Chen Guangyu co-authored Moonshot's Attention Residuals paper after Tanyue's M48 hackathon. The One Small Step track exits via funded startups, stable jobs, or commercialized projects — one student runs a 60-person company. Most teens treat college as optional. Tanyue bets judgment and transferable competencies over domain-knowledge stacking, but survived license uncertainty, hotel openings, and repeated moves — founder Jason Wang says hand-craft the first chip before the factory.
background:
Host Chen Xi leads a two-day immersion at Tanyue inside Beijing's National Tennis Center: classes, projects, MakerSpace, and interviews with founder Jason Wang, subject designers, guardians, and learners. Context is the 'super high schooler' wave — Palantir, Anthropic, and OpenAI scouting younger talent — while Tanyue surged on Chen's paper and Jiang's predictions.

Pairs with EP188's Jason Wang deep dive: this episode covers on-site mechanisms and people; the next retraces a decade of entrepreneurship and civilization questions. Tanyue began when 18-year-old Wang wrote in 2015 that AI would replace procedural jobs; opened high school in 2018; absorbed Tsinghua High International School in 2022 for full K-12.
important_facts: Mechanics and scale: ~500 students inverted pyramid (~250 high school, 100+ middle, <100 primary); no fixed rooms, schedules, or rankings; guardians/learners titles, mentors, life coaches, four houses (Chizi/Fupu/Shangshan/Wuji). ~100 courses including 21 APs, but focus is competencies — critical thinking, information literacy, creation, collaboration; Life Skill classes cover outdoor survival, cooking, first aid, and life discussions. Tuition 200,000+ RMB/year; outcomes split — Harvard/MIT/liberal arts paths alongside direct startups or niche tracks like insect art.

'One Small Step' and super high schoolers: 1+X structure — year one rebuilds learning habits; X stage 1–3 years at student pace; three exit paths are funded independent startups, stable employment income, or commercialized project transfer. Cases: Xu Haoming's smart wake-up lamp, 15-year-old Liu Yizhou's design studio, Jiang Yin's dyslexia-reading aid company (60-person team via social recruiting, 8 on core project). M48 hackathon is national, airfare/lodging covered, AI-for-Good themes; Chen Guangyu debuted at the first edition before Moonshot paper and Musk like. VCs and industry leaders judge 48-hour builds on-site.

Ten-year experiment risks: 2017 launched on training licenses for non-compulsory education; 2019 campus build stalled in pandemic — hotel openings (three sites in 2020); 'double reduction' made full-time model non-compliant, forcing move to the tennis center. Wang reflects on early arrogance — mission to 'sustain civilization' without self-cultivation first; rejected private-school mergers fearing economic-cycle dilution; personal debt and home collateral. Conclusion: not a universal answer — suits highly self-driven, disciplined students; ~500 is the right size; ideal is sharing the model, not factory-scale replication.

mental_model.name: Competency-First × Third Path × Simulator Upgrade
mental_model.components: Domain knowledge answers more questions; competencies (judgment, aesthetics, critique, collaboration) decide which questions matter. Diplomas offer low-cost consensus and platform resource access; 'One Small Step' tries to replace that with real work products. Schools simulate society's next stage — factories in the industrial era, project-based creation and lifelong learning in the AI era.
mental_model.application: Underwrite innovative education: Private:Tanyue School is a high-cost personalization bet (Long/Low) — moat is trust and graduate work chains, not scale. Private:Moonshot indirectly signals super-teen talent via hackathon pipeline. PLTR (Long/Low) and peers scouting younger talent is a new AI hiring frontier, but school models don't map linearly to public revenue; watch competency credentials and portfolio rails (GitHub-like) displacing diplomas.

key_insights.view: College is no longer the only exit.
key_insights.question: What does 'One Small Step' bet on?
key_insights.answer: AI lowers startup barriers — 48-hour hackathons validate value creation; three graduation paths require real social outcomes. Interviewed teens are fifty-fifty or skip 'conventional jobs,' seeing university as optional for skills and networks they need now.

key_insights.question: What to learn in the AI era?
key_insights.answer: Judgment, aesthetics, critical thinking — AI floods information; filtering and verification matter. Competencies transfer across domains (analysis in finance vs biotech); habits of mind resist AI distillation better than exam memorization.

key_insights.view: Innovative schools must hand-craft the first chip.
key_insights.question: Why not mainstream?
key_insights.answer: Personalization + mentors + project courses = high cost; regulatory uncertainty, moves, and debt nearly killed the school. Wang: deeply practice educational essence and hand-craft chip one before the factory; ~500 students is the responsible ceiling for families and mission.

top_investment_implications.thesis: Ten-year competency K-12 experiment — One Small Step entrepreneurship, M48 hackathon, portfolio credentials; ~500 healthy scale with VC/HR watching graduates. High tuition, hard to replicate, regulatory and debt history; trust accrues cohort-by-cohort, not internet viral growth

Chen Guangyu co-authored Attention Residuals liked by Musk — not enrolled at Tanyue but from its AI hackathon ecosystem; Moonshot paper reinforces super-high-schooler pipeline narrative tied to Kimi talent competition

Silicon Valley giants (Palantir, Anthropic, OpenAI) scout younger super talent — Tanyue grads already queried by top founders; PLTR Long on front-loaded talent locking, though school models do not linearly map to public revenue
